name: setns-nonruntime
why: setns from a non-runtime process is the container-escape namespace-join primitive
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for setns_namespace_join_behavioral.c's setns() record

name: setns-shell-escape
why: a shell in a compromised container joining a host namespace fd is the same escape from a different, non-runtime process
source: synthetic: an interactive shell calling setns toward a host namespace

name: lsns-nsget-ioctl-no-setns
why: lsns inspects namespaces with ioctl(ns_fd, NS_GET_*) but joins none; it keeps the SYSCALL surface on a namespace fd but is not setns, so the setns syscall anchor must be load-bearing. openat/ioctl of /proc/<pid>/ns/* is NOT the audited step (atomic.rules records setns, not openat), so this models the audited ioctl lsns really makes instead
source: recorded: strace of lsns on this host -- ioctl(fd, NS_GET_USERNS 0xb701); only ioctl (not openat) is in detections/audit/atomic.rules

name: unshare-new-namespace
why: unshare creates a NEW namespace rather than joining an existing one, so it is not the escape primitive; flipping only the syscall name to setns fires
source: synthetic: unshare(CLONE_NEWNS) by a non-runtime process

name: runc-rootfs-setns-allowlisted
why: runc's main process enters the new container's mount namespace during `runc run` (setns(ns_fd, CLONE_NEWNS)); this is the one setns path that runs as comm 'runc', which the comm allowlist suppresses. The high-volume container-exec path runs as comm 'runc:[1:CHILD]'/'runc:[2:INIT]', which runtime_images covers (see runc-child-memfd-image-setns-filtered)
source: recorded: strace of `runc run` (runc 1.5.1) on this host -- comm 'runc' setns(18, CLONE_NEWNS=0x20000) during rootfs setup

name: nsenter-allowlisted
why: nsenter is an allowlisted admin tool that joins namespaces by design; the allowlist must filter it
source: recorded: strace of util-linux/busybox nsenter joining a container's namespaces -- comm 'nsenter' setns(fd, CLONE_NEWNS=0x20000)

name: runc-child-memfd-image-setns-filtered
why: docker/kubectl exec through runc 1.1: runc's nsexec child (comm runc:[1:CHILD], set with prctl before join_namespaces) runs from runc's memfd re-exec image and setns()es into each of the container's namespaces; runtime_images suppresses it (the old comm-only allowlist fired on every exec)
source: runc v1.1.12 libcontainer/nsenter/cloned_binary.c (memfd_create("runc_cloned:/proc/self/exe"), fexecve) and v1.2.0 nsexec.c (prctl(PR_SET_NAME, "runc:[1:CHILD]"), then setns()); exe as in the benign corpus docker-exec template

name: runc-child-binary-setns-filtered
why: runc's nsexec child running from the installed runc binary (no memfd clone) joins the container's network namespace; the runc-binary entry of runtime_images suppresses it
source: runc v1.2.0 libcontainer/nsenter/nsexec.c: comm runc:[1:CHILD] set with prctl(PR_SET_NAME) before setns(); /usr/sbin/runc is the Debian/Ubuntu runc package path

name: snap-confine-joins-snap-mount-ns-filtered
why: snap-confine joins the snap's preserved mount namespace on every snap launch with setns(fd, CLONE_NEWNS); the snap-confine entry of runtime_images suppresses it
source: snapd cmd/snap-confine/ns-support.c: setns(mnt_fd, CLONE_NEWNS); exe as in the benign corpus snap-confine template

name: ip-netns-exec-filtered
why: `ip netns exec <name>` joins a named network namespace with setns(fd, CLONE_NEWNET); the ip entry of runtime_images suppresses it, consistent with the nsenter allowlist entry
source: iproute2 lib/namespace.c netns_switch(): setns(netns, CLONE_NEWNET); exe as in the benign corpus ip netns template

name: ip-path-joins-mount-ns
why: a binary at an allowlisted ip path that joins a MOUNT namespace still fires: the ip entry suppresses only CLONE_NEWNET joins, so a binary placed at /usr/bin/ip inside a container cannot hide a mount-namespace escape
source: synthetic: setns(fd, CLONE_NEWNS=0x20000) with exe /usr/bin/ip (exe is logged relative to the process's root, kernel fs/d_path.c d_path())

name: spoofed-runc-child-comm-from-tmp
why: a process that names itself runc:[1:CHILD] with prctl but runs from a non-runc image still fires: the runc entries require the runc binary or runc's memfd image as well as the comm
source: synthetic: prctl(PR_SET_NAME, "runc:[1:CHILD]") then setns(fd, CLONE_NEWNS) from /tmp/x

name: runc-1.2-overlayfs-child-setns-filtered
why: docker/kubectl exec through runc >= 1.2: runc executes `runc init` from its sealed overlayfs clone (a file on a detached overlay mount, which d_path and so audit's exe= render as /runc), and the nsexec child (comm runc:[1:CHILD]) setns()es into each of the container's namespaces (IPC, UTS, NET, PID, MNT). The /runc entry of runtime_images suppresses it; before that entry the rule fired five times per exec on hosts with current runc
source: recorded: runc 1.5.1 on this host, `strace -f -e trace=setns,prctl,execve -e inject=setns:delay_enter=1500000 runc exec` while polling /proc: runc:[1:CHILD] -> /runc, execve("/proc/self/fd/6", ["runc","init"]), prctl(PR_SET_NAME, "runc:[1:CHILD]"), setns(12, CLONE_NEWNET); runc v1.5.1 libcontainer/exeseal/overlayfs_linux.go sealedOverlayfs (fsmount, openat(overlayFd, binName))

name: runc-1.2-overlayfs-child-mount-ns-filtered
why: the same runc >= 1.2 exec child's last join, into the container's mount namespace (CLONE_NEWNS, a1 0x20000); the /runc entry suppresses it whatever the nstype, as runc joins every namespace of the container
source: recorded: runc 1.5.1 on this host, same strace run: setns(14, CLONE_NEWNS) from runc:[1:CHILD] with /proc/<pid>/exe /runc

name: binary-at-runc-path-wrong-comm
why: a binary at /runc whose comm is not one of runc's nsexec names still fires: the /runc entry needs runc's prctl comm as well. A process that sets both values is not caught (see the description's filter limits)
source: synthetic: setns(fd, CLONE_NEWNS) with exe /runc and comm sh, as a binary placed at /runc in a container's root would log

name: rootless-runc-child-setns-filtered
why: `docker exec` under rootless Docker: rootless runc cannot mount its sealed overlayfs clone, so it runs `runc init` from its memfd copy (exe /memfd:runc_cloned:/proc/self/exe (deleted), as runc < 1.2 always does), and the nsexec child (comm runc:[1:CHILD]) joins the container's namespaces as the user; auditd logs the user's host uid (1000), not root. The memfd entry of runtime_images has no euid condition, so it stays filtered. An unprivileged process can only join namespaces under a user namespace its own uid created, so an euid 0 condition would add this noise and stop no escape
source: recorded by the reviewer: rootless runc 1.5.1 runs runc init from /memfd:runc_cloned:/proc/self/exe (deleted); runc v1.5.1 libcontainer/exeseal/cloned_binary_linux.go CloneSelfExe (sealedOverlayfs first, then falls back to a sealed memfd copy); linux v6.8 kernel/audit.c audit_log_task_info() (uid and euid via from_kuid(&init_user_ns, ...)); setns(2) and user_namespaces(7)
